{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABY1jUxA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhCbHmU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 47, "title": "Separate immersive PC-VAN terminal operations from modern application Settings", "body": "## Problem

Issue #45 / merged PR #46 moved **every operation** into one terminal command interface, including AI model downloads, resident profile editing, color/speed preferences, JSON backup/restore, factory reset and offline storage. That interpretation went too far.

The intended distinction is **between actions that belong to PC-VAN itself and configuration of the modern browser application**:

- **Inside the PC-VAN service**: everything must be operated through the terminal's text input, including first-time *user* handle registration/selection, browsing, `WRITE`, `REPLY n`, multi-line post editing, `READ n`, navigation and in-service commands. Do **not** reintroduce composition dialogs, clickable reply-parent links, navigation helper buttons or separate user registration forms.
- **Outside the simulated service**: application settings and maintenance should be available through a compact **「設定 / Options」 button that opens a normal Settings dialog**. This includes local AI model configuration/download consent, artificial resident profile/routine/scheduling controls, display appearance/speed, backup/restore, factory reset, offline caching/storage, and technical provenance/About. Such controls are not historical PC-VAN activities, so forcing users to type commands for them is needlessly cumbersome and less discoverable.

The user's priority is **immersion within PC-VAN, with sensible modern configuration outside it**. It is not "ban every dialog throughout the browser application." This issue explicitly corrects the broader mandate in #45, which has already been marked completed.

## Expected outcome

The public experience has two clean, intentionally different interaction layers.

### 1. PC-VAN terminal (sole in-world control)

Keep the command-driven operation introduced in #45:

- First-visit optional human handle registration via terminal prompts, `HANDLE` display/selection/rename (or an equally discoverable in-terminal equivalent); unregistered `WRITE` or `REPLY` prompts the user for a handle and resumes the interrupted draft.
- MAIN, SIG exploration, LIST, READ, navigation, thread parent references as **plain text** (`返信先：#31`), `READ 31`, `WRITE`, `REPLY 31`.
- Title and line-by-line body entry, `.END`, preview, edit, explicit send confirmation and cancellation entirely in the terminal. Japanese IME and empty lines remain correct. No posting modal or floating helper elements.
- Terminal command messages remain period-appropriate and avoid routine AI/simulation/source explanations. Model and system setup dialogs must **never interrupt an in-progress title/body/confirmation prompt**.

### 2. Application Settings (clearly outside the terminal)

Restore a discreet **「設定 / Options」** control in the terminal header or adjacent browser-app chrome. Clicking it opens an accessible Settings dialog, preferably reusing suitable proven components/behavior from before #45 rather than building two independent configuration engines.

Group modern settings naturally:
- **Display / terminal presentation**: theme (white/green/amber), simulated speed, CRT effects, session information, terminal log download.
- **AI model and activity**: model selector, load/stop/progress/error, explicit heavyweight download consent, WebGPU limitations, ten individual resident profiles/routines/frequencies, overall auto-posting options and manual AI preview/generation (technical operation rather than pretending to be a historical PC-VAN command).
- **Local data / maintenance**: JSON export and import (with the native file picker and a clear replacement confirmation), **「初期状態に戻す」** with irreversibility warning and backup option, world provenance, offline app-shell/cache and storage settings.
- **About / help**: optional technical evidence and artificial authorship/provenance, clearly separate from ordinary SIG transcripts.

It is **fine to retain existing typed application shortcuts** such as `SETTINGS`, `ABOUT` or `BACKUP` if useful for keyboard users, but the Settings dialog/button must be a first-class usable path to **every application configuration feature**, not a stub. Prefer a **single underlying state/action implementation**, avoiding conflicting UI and terminal-only settings paths. Keyboard access to the Settings button and dialog is required, but **PC-VAN service participation itself remains terminal-only**.

### Model onboarding nuance

Preserve #39/#41's essential user experience: a first-time user should **notice** that a local AI model can be prepared, but ordinary UI copy should neutrally say e.g. `AIモデルの準備` / `モデルを読み込む`, **not** continually promote “10 AI residents.” A discreet neutral setup cue can link straight to the AI Settings panel and consent flow. The model's potentially hundreds-of-MB-to-GB download requires explicit, informative confirmation; opening Settings or entering PC-VAN must not start any download. Progress, errors, cancellation and “ready” state are visible in the dialog. Previously granted model consent, per-world deferral and automatic activity must be preserved.

## Context

- #45 / [PR #46](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/46) deliberately removed app dialogs and the Settings button. This Issue **supersedes only that part**, not the in-terminal user/posting state machine.
- Current `src/terminal.ts` has just terminal header, transcript and persistent command input; `src/commands.ts` hosts `TerminalCommands`, `SETTINGS/CONFIG`, command-state handling, handle/compose and app-settings menus.
- Current `src/settings.ts` is now a command-menu and provenance renderer; `src/main.ts` wires the controller, AI controls, repository and commands. `src/ai/controls.ts`, `src/ai/setup.ts`, `src/storage/controls.ts` and `src/offline/controls.ts` contain model disclosure, AI and storage/offline actions that can be shared with a dialog-driven presentation.
- Existing validated local storage, reset/restore, AI generation, cross-tab locking and prompt-safety behavior must be preserved; Settings must remain a modern app affordance, **not** a menu item inserted into the historical MAIN or a remote PC-VAN service.
- The original #31/#39/#41 UI direction emphasized a terminal-dominant display, hidden technical metadata and neutral AI setup; reconcile those principles with the terminal-only in-world work from #45.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), the [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), the [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and review guidance. English Issue/PR/docs text, Japanese product copy.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A small visible **「設定 / Options」** button exists outside the terminal transcript and opens an accessible dialog containing **functional** application-level presentation, model/activity/resident, backup/restore/reset, offline/storage and About/help settings. The terminal remains visually dominant and usable after closing the dialog.
- [ ] **No app-created dialogs or helper links for in-world activity**: first-time handle registration, handle selection, WRITE/REPLY multiline drafting/review/edit/sending, READ/LIST/forum navigation and read markers remain fully operable by typing commands; there is no clickable “返信先を読む” element or separate compose/registration form. The #45 terminal flows remain intact.
- [ ] Confirm that the model selector, load/cancel/progress, opt-in consent, ten individually editable AI profiles, scheduling parameters, cache checks, local data export/import, factory reset and offline controls all **actually execute** from Settings, not merely display a menu or direct users to type complex terminal commands. Preserve validation and permissions, especially affirmative consent to model downloads and destructive data replacement/reset.
- [ ] Application-only controls and prompts do not appear as intrusive simulated PC-VAN messages. Settings/AI dialogs must never steal focus during active terminal multiline entry, IME composition or send confirmation: open them only on deliberate user action; closing restores the draft and focuses the terminal. During a sensitive in-world prompt, either defer opening Settings or preserve and safely resume it without accidental submit/loss.
- [ ] Neutral AI model setup remains discoverable without emphasizing fictional residents; the app avoids unsolicited AI identity disclosures in normal terminal output but retains accurate author/origin/model provenance and local-only simulation details in Settings → About/Details and JSON backups.
- [ ] Settings and optional typed aliases use the **same** persisted settings and action paths (or make one route to the other) so display preferences, selected model, consent, AI status, posts, read states, reset and import stay synchronized. A Settings UI error or model-load failure must not block terminal reading/posting. Do not introduce two divergent implementations of WebLLM consent or storage mutation.
- [ ] The Settings dialog works with keyboard alone (focus entry, Tab/Shift+Tab, Escape/close, Japanese IME), is usable on desktop/mobile and respects reduced motion. The `#command` field remains the primary input when Settings is closed; current text rendering and progressive output are preserved.
- [ ] Reset/import/cross-tab change safely invalidates stale dialogs/model operations and refreshes Settings and the terminal without resurrecting old data; cached WebLLM weights and offline app shell retain their existing reset semantics.
- [ ] Add/update automated browser/controller tests for **both layers**: a complete keyboard-only human handle → READ/WRITE/REPLY journey without any app dialog, plus opening Settings and changing display options, setting up/model consenting/pausing AI, editing a resident profile, exporting/importing JSON and factory resetting via the dialog. Include cancel/refusal, active-draft protection, IME, focus, mobile width, restore/reload and mocked model failures. Preserve existing tests as applicable.
- [ ] Update README, product help and AI/storage documentation with the **explicit distinction**: PC-VAN in-world operations are terminal-only; the modern application's Settings button/dialog is the normal place for technical configuration. Report actual `npm test`, `npm run build` and other relevant checks in the PR.

## Optional validation

Manual nostalgia/UX review: read, post and reply using only the terminal, then adjust AI and screen colors through Settings without losing your position. Real WebGPU model download and physical-device/IME testing are useful but not mandatory pre-merge gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. The two-layer behavior can be checked against a local production build prior to merge; GitHub Pages publication is handled by the existing deployment workflow.
